findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names as arguments instead of shell input
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `main; arbitrary-command`, `exec` executes it with the application's privileges. Valid ref names can also contain shell metacharacters. Background commands may outlive the returned shell process, preventing callers from reliably cancelling or owning spawned work. Preserve the previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` argument boundary.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve rejection of an empty branch
findings.body: For `showBranch("")`, the previous implementation passed an empty revision and Git rejected it. The new interpolation produces `git show`, which succeeds against `HEAD`, silently returning data for the wrong revision.

findings.title: [P2] Keep `git` as the cancellable child process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns a shell process rather than the `git` process. On Windows, cancelling the returned child can terminate `cmd.exe` while a long-running `git show` descendant continues. On POSIX, valid branch names containing `&` (for example `topic&true`) are parsed as asynchronous shell control flow, allowing the shell to emit `exit` before the spawned `git` operation finishes and making subsequent cancellation ineffective. `execFile()` kept execution and lifecycle tied directly to `git`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so input such as `main; printf INJECTED` executes an additional command under the application user. Even valid Git ref names may contain shell metacharacters such as `;`; the previous `execFile` implementation passed them safely as one argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve rejection of an empty branch
findings.body:
For `showBranch("")`, the previous implementation passes an empty revision and Git exits with an error. The new command becomes `git show`, which succeeds and displays HEAD, silently converting invalid input into data for the wrong revision.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell and interpolates `branch` verbatim. Any untrusted branch value such as `HEAD; <command>` executes arbitrary OS commands with the application's privileges. The prior `execFile()` call passed the branch as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch directly to `execFile` to prevent unowned subprocesses
findings.body:
On POSIX, input such as `HEAD >/dev/null; sleep 100000 >/dev/null 2>&1 &` launches a background process through `/bin/sh`. The returned `ChildProcess` tracks only the shell, so callers cannot terminate the orphaned process; repeated calls can exhaust process and memory resources.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
